answer: Each agent identity must lock a per-identity bond in escrow, non-transferable and non-poolable, released only after a long dispute window. Reputation is a slow-decaying kernel over that identity's own settled history, not its owner's balance, so splitting one wallet into ten thousand fresh keys yields ten thousand zero-history agents that each still pay the lock. A shared vault of stake cannot back more than one identity by design. The attacker's marginal cost per key is bond plus waiting time, so a ripple of clones never becomes cheaper than real work.
